messages.content: Write a recap post about what a team learned at an industry conference. Around 250 words.

output:
Here's the draft. I've left bracketed placeholders where only your team knows the specifics — swap those and the post is ready.

---

# What we brought back from [Conference name]

Four of us spent three days at [Conference] last week. Here's what we're still talking about.

The hallway conversations were worth more than the keynotes. Two of the sessions we'd circled in advance turned out to be product pitches with a case study bolted on. Meanwhile, twenty minutes with [name] from [company] over bad coffee gave us a concrete answer to the [problem area] question we'd been going in circles on since [month]. Next year we're budgeting time for that on purpose instead of treating it as slack between sessions.

On the technical side, the thing that surprised us was how many teams have quietly moved off [approach A]. We assumed we were behind. We're not. Of the six teams we asked, four are running something close to what we built last quarter, and two of them hit the same wall we did around [specific limit]. That's reassuring, and it also means the workaround we wrote is probably worth publishing.

The talk we'd recommend to everyone is [speaker]'s on [topic]. It's the only one that showed numbers from a real system under load rather than a diagram. Recording is at [link].

One thing we got wrong: we split up to cover more ground and ended up with four sets of notes nobody has read. Next time, one shared doc, written during the sessions.

Happy to walk anyone through the notes if [topic] is on your roadmap.

---

Comes in at 249 words.
